provenance: Authored from the frozen runbook content; no evaluation question text is used as description input.

descriptions.RB-F01-F02@1.0.0#symptoms: Recognize provider rate limiting, outages and transport failures; distinguish explicit HTTP 429 rejection from potentially unknown 5xx or timeout delivery.
descriptions.RB-F01-F02@1.0.0#evidence-needed: For provider failure diagnosis, collect request phase, status, retry delay, all attempt outcomes, completion time, execution and predecessor state, and fingerprints.
descriptions.RB-F01-F02@1.0.0#read-only-investigation: Investigate provider failures without probing: determine pre-send failure, explicit rejection or ambiguous post-send outcome from recorded context and execution evidence.
descriptions.RB-F01-F02@1.0.0#allowed-remediation: For provider outages or throttling, operators may restore connectivity or reduce pressure; a proven Telegram 429 permits recording a conservative cooldown and later investigation.
descriptions.RB-F01-F02@1.0.0#forbidden-actions: Provider-failure investigation prohibits infrastructure restarts, provider calls, credential disclosure, payload rewrites and treating leases or 5xx responses as proof of delivery or rejection.
descriptions.RB-F01-F02@1.0.0#replay-and-approval: Provider failures have no Phase 5 replay; future Telegram send-stage 429 consideration needs complete evidence, unchanged inputs, ordering and safety gates, and owner approval.
descriptions.RB-F01-F02@1.0.0#verification-rollback-o: Verify captured retry timestamps without sending; conflicting evidence or unproven provider recovery requires abstention and escalation, with configuration rollback through normal controls.
descriptions.RB-F01-F02@1.0.0#simulated-example: Illustrative fabricated Telegram 429 with retry_after 30; this retrieval example supplies no real incident evidence or replay permission.
descriptions.RB-F01-F02@1.0.0#sources: Source references for provider rate-limit and transport-failure guidance: taxonomy, master plan and Telegram handler; current code and policy take precedence.
descriptions.RB-F03-F04@1.0.0#symptoms: Recognize credential or destination symptoms: missing configured secrets, 401/403, inaccessible Telegram chats, invalid email destinations and username resolution errors.
descriptions.RB-F03-F04@1.0.0#evidence-needed: Credential and destination diagnosis requires redacted presence and source information, provider phase/status, destination structure, missing template paths, fingerprints and prior delivery outcomes.
descriptions.RB-F03-F04@1.0.0#read-only-investigation: Validate credential and destination inputs without exposing values; distinguish missing action fields from unknown worker fallback and destination resolution from send failure.
descriptions.RB-F03-F04@1.0.0#allowed-remediation: Credential and destination repair belongs to authorized operators: rotate or configure credentials, repair membership or permissions, and reinvestigate corrected workflow configuration.
descriptions.RB-F03-F04@1.0.0#forbidden-actions: Credential and destination investigation must never request, display, store, test or transmit secrets, send test messages, mutate destinations or equate credential repair with replay approval.
descriptions.RB-F03-F04@1.0.0#replay-and-approval: Credential and destination repairs are manual and Phase 5 replay is unavailable; later replay separately requires resolved delivery uncertainty, unchanged inputs, policy and owner approval.
descriptions.RB-F03-F04@1.0.0#verification-rollback-o: Verify only credential presence and operator permission evidence; unknown worker fallback or delivery requires abstention, with credential-manager rollback and destination-owner escalation.
descriptions.RB-F03-F04@1.0.0#simulated-example: Fabricated missing configured bot token, unknown worker environment and Telegram 403 illustrate uncertainty and operator repair rather than secret discovery.
descriptions.RB-F03-F04@1.0.0#sources: Credential and destination references include taxonomy, action documentation and Telegram/email handlers; deterministic code and policy govern interpretation.
descriptions.RB-F04-F06@1.0.0#symptoms: Recognize input, registry and ordering faults: missing template paths, incorrect field types, unsupported action types, missing runs, gapped or duplicate stages and unowned events.
descriptions.RB-F04-F06@1.0.0#evidence-needed: Validation and registry diagnosis requires redacted validation, current action type and deployed registry, run/stage identity, ordered predecessors, provenance and fingerprints; historical definitions may be unavailable.
descriptions.RB-F04-F06@1.0.0#read-only-investigation: Apply deterministic validation, report missing template paths that become empty strings, compare action types with deployed email/telegram handlers, and inspect contiguous stage ordering.
descriptions.RB-F04-F06@1.0.0#allowed-remediation: Operators may repair producer data or workflow definitions for future runs; engineering may align seeded action IDs and deployed handlers before reinvestigation.
descriptions.RB-F04-F06@1.0.0#forbidden-actions: Validation forbids inventing identities, assigning orphan events to users, generating handlers, editing the registry, rewriting historical payloads, bypassing stage checks or calling providers.
descriptions.RB-F04-F06@1.0.0#replay-and-approval: Invalid input, changed input, orphaned events and unsupported handlers remain replay-blocked in read-only Phase 5; deployment and inputs must be verified separately.
descriptions.RB-F04-F06@1.0.0#verification-rollback-o: Verify parser semantics, registry and stage order without execution; missing historical snapshots, ambiguous ordering and producer schema faults require engineering escalation.
descriptions.RB-F04-F06@1.0.0#simulated-example: Fabricated missing customer.channel template path and unsupported slack action illustrate two validation findings without authority to add a handler or modify a run.
descriptions.RB-F04-F06@1.0.0#sources: Input and registry references link taxonomy, worker parser, validation and action registry; code takes precedence.
descriptions.RB-F07@1.0.0#symptoms: Recognize unknown external delivery after a lost provider response or terminal database write, missing receipt or expired lease; worker ownership does not prove delivery.
descriptions.RB-F07@1.0.0#evidence-needed: Unknown-delivery diagnosis needs every attempt outcome, provider phase and safe receipt, request/action fingerprints, lease/completion state, fencing and provider reconciliation.
descriptions.RB-F07@1.0.0#read-only-investigation: Reconstruct observations across the provider boundary and separate action failure from persistence failure; transport errors, invalid responses and expired pending executions remain unknown without independent evidence.
descriptions.RB-F07@1.0.0#allowed-remediation: Preserve unknown-delivery evidence for operator reconciliation; engineering can improve capture or fencing, while email reconsideration needs identical request/key within verified provider deduplication timing.
descriptions.RB-F07@1.0.0#forbidden-actions: Unknown-delivery rules forbid resending Telegram, reclaiming leases for another call, deleting executions or resetting status; approval and changed or expired idempotency keys cannot resolve uncertainty.
descriptions.RB-F07@1.0.0#replay-and-approval: Unknown Telegram delivery blocks replay; deferred email replay requires verified guarantees, identical request/key, captured timing, deterministic policy and separate owner approval.
descriptions.RB-F07@1.0.0#verification-rollback-or-es: Retain unknown delivery until authorized provider receipt reconciliation proves the outcome; missing receipts and stale workers need engineering escalation, and accepted external effects have no safe rollback.
descriptions.RB-F07@1.0.0#simulated-example: Fabricated sent Telegram request, dropped response and expired lease demonstrate unknown delivery despite no database success receipt.
descriptions.RB-F07@1.0.0#sources: Unknown-delivery references include taxonomy, idempotency documentation, execution store and provider terms; current code and guarantees govern safety.
descriptions.RB-F08@1.0.0#symptoms: Recognize duplicate failures or investigations, stale proposals, terminal FAILED and requests to repeat or reset SUCCESS; duplicate broker delivery grants no new authority.
descriptions.RB-F08@1.0.0#evidence-needed: Duplicate and stale-state investigation needs canonical case/failure IDs, execution and lease state, source reference, evidence versions/fingerprints, adjacent stages and approval/replay identities.
descriptions.RB-F08@1.0.0#read-only-investigation: Deduplicate source references, read current state and compare versions/fingerprints to distinguish new failures from stale or resolved investigations without execution writes.
descriptions.RB-F08@1.0.0#allowed-remediation: Operators may close or supersede duplicate investigations; a future deterministic replay service can create one durable intent only after every gate, with manual escalation until then.
descriptions.RB-F08@1.0.0#forbidden-actions: Terminal-state safeguards prohibit resetting SUCCESS, reopening FAILED, raw-event republication, deduplication evasion, expired approvals, fingerprint changes and retrieved-text replay authority.
descriptions.RB-F08@1.0.0#replay-and-approval: Future replay needs an unexpired approval, unchanged evidence/inputs, valid ordering, no competing or live execution, provider safety, cooldown and bounded replay count; unknowns deny.
descriptions.RB-F08@1.0.0#verification-rollback-or-es: Recheck current execution state before decisions; conflicts are no-ops or blocks and inconsistent identities/history need engineering escalation, with no Phase 5 execution-write rollback.
descriptions.RB-F08@1.0.0#simulated-example: Fabricated duplicate Kafka message asks to reset a SUCCESS stage; the example requires refusal even when the message claims approval.
descriptions.RB-F08@1.0.0#sources: Duplicate and replay-safety references include master plan, taxonomy, worker orchestration and execution store; deterministic policy governs authority.
descriptions.RB-F09-F10@1.0.0#symptoms: Recognize missing or split DLQ evidence, unpublished successors after SUCCESS, legacy gaps and historical email SDK errors that may have been recorded as success.
descriptions.RB-F09-F10@1.0.0#evidence-needed: Publication and legacy-gap diagnosis needs linked execution/failure IDs, claim/ack state, dlqPublishedAt, attempt provenance, stage/successor state, safe receipt metadata and reconciliation results.
descriptions.RB-F09-F10@1.0.0#read-only-investigation: Identify complete, partial and unavailable sources; distinguish failure publication repair from stage progression and external-action repetition while preserving historical SUCCESS.
descriptions.RB-F09-F10@1.0.0#allowed-remediation: An existing deterministic reconciler may publish stored failures by stable failure ID; engineering may repair progression or provider-result normalization, while missing evidence requires abstention.
descriptions.RB-F09-F10@1.0.0#forbidden-actions: DLQ and progression investigation prohibits fabricated errors, reinterpreting SUCCESS from substrings, action replay to repair progression, bulk republication and raw provider response exposure.
descriptions.RB-F09-F10@1.0.0#replay-and-approval: Missing evidence, historical email uncertainty and SUCCESS block replay; deterministic progression recovery is separate from action replay approval.
descriptions.RB-F09-F10@1.0.0#verification-rollback-o: Verify shared failure-ID visibility and stage state; irrecoverable evidence loss, hidden SDK outcomes and broker/database contradictions require engineering escalation, with deployment rollback rather than deletion.
descriptions.RB-F09-F10@1.0.0#simulated-example: Fabricated SUCCESS stage with an unpublished successor and old email-error log needs separate progression and evidence review, not status rewriting or resending.
descriptions.RB-F09-F10@1.0.0#sources: DLQ and legacy-gap references include taxonomy, Kafka documentation, publisher, reconciler and email handler; current code takes precedence.
descriptions.RB-R2-COOLDOWN@1.0.0#cooldown-evidence: Calculate Telegram 429 cooldown from captured response time and retry_after, check all earlier attempt outcomes and ordering, and escalate missing clocks or contradictory delivery evidence without scheduling retries.
descriptions.RB-R2-DESTINATION@1.0.0#destination-perm: Diagnose Telegram bot removal, lost channel posting access or migrated chat IDs using captured safe codes and validation; owners repair access, without secret retrieval, joining chats or test sends.
descriptions.RB-R2-EMAIL-REJECT@1.0.0#email-rejection: Investigate email authentication or recipient rejection and swallowed SDK errors conflicting with SUCCESS through redacted status and validation; require owner repair or provider reconciliation, never test email or unsupported replay.
descriptions.RB-R2-EMAIL-UNKNOWN@1.0.0#lost-acknowled: Treat email socket loss after send, timeout or expired lease as unknown delivery; inspect attempt history and reconcile provider receipts rather than resending, polling or inferring certainty from SUCCESS.
descriptions.RB-R2-ORDERING@1.0.0#predecessor-orderin: Verify completed predecessor states rather than numeric stage index, distinguish out-of-order from duplicate terminal delivery, and preserve DAG order without resetting executions or retrying successors to fill gaps.
descriptions.RB-R2-PUBLICATION@1.0.0#publication-reco: Diagnose unpublished durable DLQ outbox records during Kafka outage or lost acknowledgement separately from action outcome; retain stable identities and escalate stuck publication without restarting brokers or marking records published.
